settings.text:
Skinbiotic+ is a dermatologist-formulated daily synbiotic designed to support gut health and the gut-skin connection.

It pairs organic inulin, a prebiotic fiber, with five probiotic organisms, so the formula supports both sides of the intestinal environment: the fuel and the organisms.

One capsule, once a day
Full ingredient transparency

settings.heading: A synbiotic for the gut-skin connection.
settings.body:
Skinbiotic+ combines a prebiotic with probiotic organisms in a single daily capsule. The prebiotic, organic inulin, is a fermentable fiber that can serve as food for certain intestinal microorganisms. The probiotic blend adds five organisms selected for their roles in gut ecology.

The formulation rationale is the pairing: fuel and organisms working together in the intestinal environment, where much of the conversation between gut and skin begins.
settings.quote: Prebiotic fuel. Probiotic organisms. One daily capsule.

settings.heading: What is the gut-skin axis?
settings.body:
The gut-skin axis describes communication between the intestinal environment and the skin. Researchers study several pathways, including microbial metabolites, immune signaling, barrier integrity, and systemic metabolism.

The concept has substantial biological support. Outcomes still vary by organism, dose, and population, so we describe the research carefully and do not generalize it.
settings.takeaway: Skinbiotic+ is designed to support the gut side of that conversation.

settings.heading: What makes it a synbiotic?
settings.body: A synbiotic pairs a prebiotic with probiotics. Each side has a different job, and the formula is built around having both.

settings.body: Organic inulin at 500 mg and a 215 mg probiotic blend, as listed on the label.

settings.name: Organic inulin
settings.text: A fermentable fiber that serves as food for certain intestinal microorganisms. It forms the prebiotic foundation of the formula.

settings.name: Lactobacillus plantarum
settings.amount: Part of the 215 mg probiotic blend
settings.text: A widely studied species. Research is strain-specific, so findings on one strain are not assumed to apply to every L. plantarum.

settings.name: Bifidobacterium lactis
settings.amount: Part of the 215 mg probiotic blend
settings.text: A Bifidobacterium species included for its role in the intestinal microbial community alongside the other organisms.

settings.name: Lactobacillus rhamnosus
settings.amount: Part of the 215 mg probiotic blend
settings.text: A Lactobacillus species studied across many gut-health contexts. Different strains behave differently.

settings.name: Bifidobacterium bifidum
settings.amount: Part of the 215 mg probiotic blend
settings.text: A Bifidobacterium species that is part of the human intestinal community, included to broaden the range of organisms in the formula.

settings.name: Akkermansia muciniphila (Akk11®)
settings.amount: Part of the 215 mg probiotic blend
settings.text: A mucus-layer-associated organism that is an active area of microbiome research. The evidence is earlier-stage than for the other organisms.

settings.heading: How the formula works together.
settings.note: This describes formulation rationale. Skinbiotic+ as a finished product has not been established here as clinically tested for these combined outcomes.

settings.title: Fuel and organisms
settings.text: Inulin supplies fermentable fiber while the probiotic blend supplies the organisms. The pairing is the design.

settings.title: Different organisms, different roles
settings.text: Species occupy different niches and produce different metabolites. The rationale is breadth, not assuming each organism does the same thing.

settings.title: An emerging addition
settings.text: Akkermansia muciniphila is included as an organism of active research interest, labeled as emerging research.

settings.heading: A community, not a single ingredient.
settings.body:
The intestinal microbiome is a community of trillions of microorganisms. It varies between people and shifts with diet, routine, and environment.

Balance in that community is a function of diversity, the fiber available to feed it, and the organisms present. That is why Skinbiotic+ is built as a pairing rather than a single probiotic.

settings.heading: What fermentation produces.
settings.body: When gut microbes ferment dietary fibers such as inulin, they produce short-chain fatty acids, including acetate, propionate, and butyrate. These molecules are studied for their roles in intestinal and systemic signaling.
settings.takeaway: Short-chain fatty acids are one pathway researchers examine within the gut-skin axis.

settings.heading: Where gut and skin research meet.
settings.body:
The skin barrier helps regulate water loss and acts as a boundary with the environment. Gut-skin research explores whether microbial signals and metabolites relate to barrier-supporting pathways.

This area is active and not settled. Skinbiotic+ is designed to support the intestinal environment; it is not a barrier product and does not make barrier claims.

settings.question: What is Skinbiotic+?
settings.answer: Skinbiotic+ is a dermatologist-formulated dietary supplement that pairs organic inulin with five probiotic organisms to support gut health and the gut-skin connection.

settings.question: What is a synbiotic?
settings.answer: A synbiotic combines a prebiotic, which feeds certain intestinal microorganisms, with probiotics, which are the organisms themselves.

settings.question: What is the gut-skin axis?
settings.answer: It describes communication between the intestinal environment and the skin through pathways such as microbial metabolites, immune signaling, and barrier integrity. Research is active and outcomes vary.

settings.question: What is Akkermansia muciniphila, and why is it labeled emerging research?
settings.answer: It is a mucus-layer-associated gut organism of growing research interest. The evidence is earlier-stage than for other components, so we label it as emerging research.

settings.question: Can I take Skinbiotic+ with UV Shield+ or Dermaboost+?

settings.question: Does Skinbiotic+ replace sunscreen?
settings.answer: No. Skinbiotic+ is not sunscreen. Continue your sun-safe habits.
